note: Taking dependency 1.1 as given, min_{1 <= j <= m} n_j <= n_i holds for each i. This node multiplies that inequality through by p_i. The ambient hypothesis states each p_i is a positive real, and multiplication by a positive real is order-preserving on R (a <= b and c > 0 imply c*a <= c*b), so p_i * min_{1 <= j <= m} n_j <= p_i * n_i for every i. The step is a single valid application of that order axiom, quantified over the same finite index set as 1.1, so no quantifier is dropped or widened. Note the positivity hypothesis is used only through p_i >= 0 here — the inference would remain sound for nonnegative p_i — so the step is if anything more conservative than needed, not overreaching. The n_i being possibly negative is harmless, since the argument never divides or changes sign.
